questions.question: Namita deposited ₹9,000 which amounted to ₹10,200 after 3 years at simple interest per annum. Had the interest been 2% more, what amount (in ₹) would she get?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹9,000

Amount (A) = ₹10,200

Time (T) = 3 years

Simple Interest (SI) = A - P = ₹10,200 - ₹9,000 = ₹1,200

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100

New Simple Interest Rate = Old Rate + 2%

New Amount = Principal + New Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

Let's find the old interest rate first:

⇒ ₹1,200 = (₹9,000 × R × 3) / 100

⇒ 120,000 = 27,000R

⇒ R = 120,000 / 27,000

⇒ R = 40/9%

New Interest Rate = 40/9% + 2% = 58/9%

New Simple Interest:

⇒ SI = (₹9,000 × 58/9 × 3) / 100

⇒ SI = ₹1,740

New Amount:

⇒ A = ₹9,000 + ₹1,740

⇒ A = ₹10,740

**The amount Namita would get if the interest rate had been 2% more is ₹10,740.**

questions.question: P and Q can finish a work individually in 30 and 45 days, respectively. P starts the work and works alone for 5 days. Then Q joins him and they work together for 6 days, after which P leaves. The part of the work left at that point is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P can finish the work in = 30 days

Q can finish the work in = 45 days

P works alone for 5 days

Then P and Q work together for 6 days

Then P leaves

**Formula used:**

Use LCM of 30 and 45 to assume total work

**Calculation:**

LCM(30, 45) = 90 units (Assume total work = 90 units)

P's 1 day work = (90)/(30) = 3 units/day

Q's 1 day work = (90)/(45) = 2 units/day

P works for 5 days: 5 × 3 = 15 units

P + Q work together for 6 days: 6 × (3 + 2) = 6 ×5 = 30 units

Total work done = 15 + 30 = 45 units

Work left = 90 - 45 = 45 units

Fraction of work left = (45)/(90) = (1)/(2) = 0.5

**∴ The part of the work left is 0.5.**

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle whose sides are of lengths 9 cm, 40 cm and 41 cm?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sides of the triangle are 9 cm, 40 cm, and 41 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a right-angled triangle = (1/2) × base × height

**Calculation:**

In the given triangle, the sides 9 cm and 40 cm can be considered as the base and height respectively, because the hypotenuse (longest side) is 41 cm.

Area = (1/2) × base × height

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 9 cm × 40 cm

⇒ Area = (1/2) × 360 cm²

⇒ Area = 180 cm²

**The area of the triangle is 180 cm².**

questions.question: If 66 cm³ of silver is drawn into a wire having a diameter of 2 mm, then the length of the wire, in m, will be: (Use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Volume of silver, V = 66 cm³

Diameter of the wire, d = 2 mm = 0.2 cm

Radius of the wire, r = d/2 = 0.1 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder, V = πr²h

Where,

π = 22/7

r = radius

h = height (or length of the wire)

**Calculation:**

Using the formula for the volume of a cylinder, we have:

66 = (22/7) × (0.1)² × h

Simplifying the equation:

⇒ 66 = (22/7) × 0.01 × h

⇒ 66 = (22/700) × h

⇒ 3 = (1/700) × h

⇒ h = 2100

Convert the length from cm to m:

⇒ h = 2100 / 100

⇒ h = 21 m

**The length of the wire is approximately 21 m.**

questions.question: A train moving at uniform speed crosses a pole in 3 seconds and a 700 m long bridge in 10 seconds. What is the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken to cross a pole = 3 sec

Time taken to cross a 700 m bridge = 10 sec

**Formula used:**

Speed = frac{{Distance}}{{Time}} 

When crossing a bridge: Distance = Length of train + Length of bridge

**Calculation:**

Let length of train = L meters

Train crosses pole in 3 sec ⇒ L = Speed × 3

Train crosses 700 m bridge in 10 sec ⇒ L + 700 = Speed × 10

From first equation: L = 3 × Speed

Substitute in second:

⇒ 3 × Speed + 700 = 10 × Speed

⇒ 700 = 10 × Speed - 3 × Speed = 7 × Speed

⇒ Speed = (700)/(7) = 100 m/s

**∴ Speed of the train = 100 m/s**

questions.question: Simplify (6.1 times 6.1 times 6.1-1)/(6.1 times 6.1+6.1+1)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The given expression follows the algebraic pattern: (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²) = a − b.

Here, replacing a with 6.1 and b with 1 perfectly matches the terms in the question.

Directly calculating a − b gives the final result.

Result = 6.1 − 1 = 5.1

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (6.1 × 6.1 × 6.1 − 1) ÷ (6.1 × 6.1 + 6.1 + 1)

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Numerator = (6.1)³ − 1³

⇒ Denominator = (6.1)² + 6.1 × 1 + 1²

⇒ Expression = [(6.1)³ − 1³] ÷ [(6.1)² + 6.1 + 1]

⇒ Applying the formula for the difference of cubes in the numerator:

⇒ Expression = [(6.1 − 1)((6.1)² + 6.1 × 1 + 1²)] ÷ [(6.1)² + 6.1 + 1]

⇒ The term ((6.1)² + 6.1 + 1) is common in both numerator and denominator.

⇒ Canceling the common term, we are left with:

⇒ Expression = 6.1 − 1

⇒ Expression = 5.1

**∴ The correct answer is 5.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Formula

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). This identity is frequently used to rapidly simplify fraction expressions containing positive cubic terms.

Difference of Squares Formula

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b). It helps in instantly factoring and reducing fractions containing squared differences.

Perfect Square Formulas

(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b². These are primary tools for algebraic expansion and solving polynomial equations.

questions.question: The average of the prime numbers between 57 and 99 (both inclusive) is: (Rounded off to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the average of the prime numbers between 57 and 99 (both inclusive).

**Formula Used:**

Average of prime numbers = (Sum of prime numbers) / (Number of prime numbers)

**Calculation:**

Prime numbers between 57 and 99 are: 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89, 97

Sum of these prime numbers = 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97

Sum of prime numbers = 679

Number of prime numbers = 9

Average of prime numbers = 679 / 9

Average of prime numbers = 75.4

**The average of the prime numbers between 57 and 99 (both inclusive) is 75.4.**

questions.question: The ratio of the sixth and seventh terms of the sequence 1, 3, 6, 10, … is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Sequence: 1, 3, 6, 10, …

**Formula Used:**

n-th term of the sequence, T_n = (n(n+1))/(2)

**Calculation:**

Sixth term, T₆ :

T₆ = (6(6+1))/(2)

T₆ = (6 times 7)/(2)

T₆ = 21

Seventh term, T₇ :

T₇ = (7(7+1))/(2) 

T₇ = (7 times 8)/(2)

T₇ = 28

Ratio of sixth and seventh terms, (T₆)/(T₇) :

(21)/(28) = (3)/(4)

**The ratio of the sixth and seventh terms of the sequence is 3 ∶ 4.**

questions.question: A book is sold at three successive discounts of 20%, 30% and 10%. The net discount in percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Three successive discounts: 20%, 30%, and 10%

**Formula used:**

Successive Discount Formula:

Net Discount % = A + B + C - (AB + AC + BC)/100 + (ABC)/10000

Where A = 20, B = 30, C = 10

**Calculation:**

Net Discount % = 20 + 30 + 10 - (20×30 + 20×10 + 30×10)/100 + (20×30×10)/10000

⇒ = 60 - (600 + 200 + 300)/100 + 6000/10000

⇒ = 60 - 11 + 0.6 = 49.6%

**∴ The net discount is 49.6%.**

questions.question: A moneylender borrows money at 4% per annum and pays the interest at the end of the year. He lends it at 8% per annum compound interest, compounded half-yearly, and receives the interest at the end of the year. In this way, he gains ₹166.4 a year. Find the amount of money he borrows.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Borrowing Rate = 4% per annum.

Lending Rate = 8% per annum compounded half-yearly.

Gain = ₹166.4 per year.

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Formula for half-yearly = A = P (1 + (r)/(2 times 100))²t 

Simple Interest Formula = SI = (P times r times t)/(100)

**Calculation:**

Let the amount of money borrowed be ₹P.

Interest paid at the end of the year = (P times 4 times 1)/(100) = 0.04P

Interest received at the end of the year (compounded half-yearly) = P (1 + (8)/(2 times 100))² - P

Interest received = P (1 + 0.04)² - P

Interest received = P (1.04²) - P 

Interest received = P (1.0816) - P

Interest received = 1.0816P - P

Interest received = 0.0816P

Gain = Interest received - Interest paid

₹166.4 = 0.0816P - 0.04P

₹166.4 = 0.0416P

⇒ P = (166.4)/(0.0416)

⇒ P = 4000

**The amount of money he borrows is ₹4,000.**
